data.name: All Stocks
data.description: Every stock in the universe, with no pattern test at all — the starting point rather than a setup. What comes back is exactly what the Filters panel lets through, so clearing the filters lists the whole EQ universe and tightening them turns this into a screen of your own. Sorted by market cap, largest first.

data.name: Trend Template
data.description: Stocks in a confirmed uptrend, judged by a stack of independent structural conditions rather than a label: a rising moving-average stack, distance off the lows, proximity to the highs and relative strength against the market. Nothing carries over from previous bars, so the verdict depends only on today's structure. Lower Min conditions to catch leaders still setting up — the Failed column names what is missing.

Young bases on the daily chart: a resistance level set 4 weeks to 4 months ago that has capped a real rally, never been closed above, and price is now back within three ADRs of. The base under it fell no more than 8.5 of its 100-day ADRs (and never over 35%) and has turned back at most three breakout tries.
data.name: Daily Base

data.description: Longer bases on the weekly chart: a resistance level set 4 to 18 months ago that has capped a real rally, never been closed above, and price is now back within three ADRs of. The base under it fell no more than 8.5 of its 100-day ADRs (and never over 45%) and has turned back at most three breakout tries.
data.name: Weekly Base

data.description: Resistance levels with price right up against them — no more than one ADR below the level, so a stock that moves 3% a day must be within 3%, one that moves 6% within 6%. The level has capped a real rally, held for a while, and not been closed above.
data.name: Near Pivot
Recent Breakout
data.description: The other side of Daily and Weekly Base — same definition of a level, but these have already gone through it, on a close with conviction volume, and are now trading clear of the level rather than still inside its noise band. Age 0 broke today; Since Break is what has already been given away.

data.name: 4% Breakout
data.description: Today's genuine movers: a big up close on volume that was both heavier than yesterday's and well above the stock's own norm, in names large and liquid enough to trade. A single-session scan — the bar is the signal — so it opens with no other filters applied; add your own from the Filters panel.

data.name: 20-SMA Pullback
data.description: Recent leaders that have come back to rest on their 20-day average with the short-term trend still intact — the spot a trend trader buys, rather than the breakout day everyone else does. Opens with no other filters applied; add your own from the Filters panel.

data.name: 50-EMA Pullback
data.description: Stocks in a strong, established uptrend that have paused and drifted back to their 50-day EMA: well off the lows, still up handsomely over the half-year, but going nowhere on the month. The deeper cousin of the 20-SMA Pullback. Opens with no other filters applied; add your own from the Filters panel.

data.name: VCP
data.description: Volatility Contraction Pattern — successive pullbacks off a confirmed pivot high, each shallower than the last, coiling back under the pivot. Runs only on stocks that already pass the full Trend Template, and is shown for a few sessions after the final contraction confirms, then dropped.

params.label: Third fall: max distance below pivot(%)

data.name: Flag Pattern
data.description: Bullish flags and pennants off a zigzag, from the "Bullish Flags — Retracement Filter" study: a five-pivot consolidation whose highs and lows each sit on a straight line that candles respect, classified as a falling channel or wedge (flag) or a contracting triangle (pennant), hanging off a pole the zigzag can trace back. The flag may give back at most 40% of the pole, measured on actual candles. Detected on the bar the flag's last pivot printed; Status says where price is now against the flag's lines. On top of the study: ₹1 Cr traded today and 20-SMA > 50-EMA > 200-SMA. The pattern is drawn on the chart the way the study draws it.

data.name: New RS before Price
data.description: Stocks whose RS line (vs NIFTY MidSmallcap 400) made a fresh high while price did not — strength showing up in the ratio before the price chart. Defaults to a dot on the current bar only.

data.name: Results Today
data.description: Stocks declaring quarterly results today: a results board meeting on NSE's calendar for today, or a result already filed with NSE today. Status is Out (with the filing time) once the filing is up, else Due. Filings are checked every 30 minutes. Empty on days with no results meetings, such as weekends.

data.name: Earnings Gap
data.description: Gapped up on results, held the gap through the session rather than being sold into, and has never filled it since. Scored on the session on or after the declaration and the one after it.

params.label: Gap held at close (1 = close ≥ open)

data.name: Episodic Pivot
data.description: A big up close on results that finished near the top of the day's range — a strong close, not a spike that was sold into. Scored on the session on or after the declaration and the one after it.

data.name: EPS Doublers
data.description: The blowout quarter, read off the P&L rather than the chart: EPS, sales and net profit all up sharply together against the same quarter a year earlier — never the previous one, because Indian quarters are seasonal. All three are required at once, since EPS alone can jump on a buyback or a one-off, and sales alone on an acquisition that earns nothing. Growth is only counted off a meaningful positive base; drop Min base EPS to 0 to see the turnarounds. Listed for 30 sessions after the result was declared, freshest first.

data.name: Stage 2 Breakout
data.description: The TrendStage Pro 'Power Breakout' — the indicator our stage column comes from: a close above the highest high of the previous 50 sessions, on at least 2x the 20-day average volume, closing in the top quarter of the day's range, with the stock in Stage 2 (Uptrend) and fresh to it — entered Stage 2 in the 5 sessions before, or came into this Stage 2 run straight from Stage 1 (Basing) or Stage 3. Breakouts in the last 7 sessions, freshest first. RMV before is the base's tightness the day before the break (under 25 = tight); set Max RMV to 25 for breakouts out of tight bases only.

data.name: Code 33
data.description: Code 33: over the last three reported quarters, sales growth, EPS growth and net margin each rose quarter after quarter — e.g. sales 12% → 18% → 27%, EPS 20% → 34% → 58%, margin 8.1% → 8.9% → 10.2%. Growth is always against the same quarter a year earlier, because Indian quarters are seasonal. Guardrails: every growth figure positive and the latest EPS growth at least 20%; year-ago EPS at least ₹0.50 (a tiny or loss-making base makes the % meaningless — losses are under Turnarounds); EPS restated for splits and bonuses, or growth taken from net profit where the share history does not line up; one basis per stock (consolidated, else standalone); a one-off tax-credit quarter left out.

data.name: EPS Accelerators
data.description: EPS growth rising three quarters running (e.g. 20% → 34% → 58%) on growing sales — the wider net of Code 33, without the margin test. Same year-on-year reading and the same guardrails: positive growth, latest EPS growth at least 20%, year-ago EPS at least ₹0.50, splits and bonuses adjusted, one basis per stock, one-off tax credits left out.

data.name: Turnarounds
data.description: A loss in the same quarter a year ago, a profit now — on sales up at least 10% — with net profit improving in each of the last three quarters. A % growth off a loss means nothing, so these are kept out of the accelerator scans and listed here. One-off tax-credit profits are left out.

data.name: High Volume
data.description: Stocks that just printed a volume event — a bar clearing their own highest volume ever (HVE), of the last year (HVY) or of the last quarter (HVQ). Ranked against the stock's own history, not a flat multiple of average, and only counted when the bar stands alone. Volume is direction-blind, so the bar must also have closed strong and moved — volume that arrived with a move, not a sell-off.

data.name: New Listing (IPO)
data.description: Stocks listed within the last year, read against the only structure they have — the high and low since listing. A small From High is the IPO base; pair it with High Age to tell a base from a fresh spike. Listing date is NSE's, IPOs only: a company that was already public elsewhere before its NSE listing is not counted as new.

data.name: IPO Base
data.description: Recent listings still inside their first base and coiled just under its level — the breakout has not happened yet. Day two decides the level: if it held under the listing-day high, that high is the resistance (C2); if it broke it, the first pivot high above the listing high is (C1). A base has six months and a 35% fall ends it; a close through the level ends it too, so what is listed here is only what is still waiting.

data.name: Tight Range
data.description: Two tight-range scans side by side, one list. Tight Setups: a hit on any of three methods — two measure a box against the stock's own daily range, the third is a run of closes in a narrow band on a contracting range — behind a trend filter and a 3-month gain gate. RTI: three or more bars in a row each among the narrowest of its last five (RTI ≤ 18), boxed inside 5.5%, with 20-SMA > 50-EMA > 200-SMA, the close within 5% of the 20-SMA, ₹1 Cr traded today and a 500–80,000 Cr cap band. Method says which scan found it.

data.name: 1M Gainers
data.description: Stocks that have made a big move over the last month, screened down to names liquid enough to trade. No pattern test — the move is the signal, and the rest of the screen keeps out the microcaps that dominate any raw sorted-by-return list.

data.name: 3M Gainers
data.description: Stocks that have made a big move over the last quarter, screened down to names liquid enough to trade. The slower cousin of 1M Gainers — a quarter of advance is a trend rather than a burst.

data.name: Outperformers
data.description: Stocks beating the rest of the market this week, this month and this quarter: 1-week RS Rating above 90, 1-month above 85 and 3-month above 80, among names liquid enough to trade (30-session median turnover of ₹1 Cr or more and a price of ₹5 or more). Strongest 1M RS first.

data.name: Doublers
data.description: Stocks that have doubled or better over the past year, screened down to names liquid enough to trade. No pattern test — a year of doubling is the signal; the leaders of the cycle are on this list long before they are on the front page.

data.name: Big Reversal
data.description: Stocks in a clean, fully stacked downtrend that turned in a single session: a violent up bar on a surge of volume that held most of its gains into the close. The strict downtrend test is what separates a change of character from a bounce in a stock that was already drifting sideways. Signals from the last few sessions, freshest first — Since Signal shows what has already been given away.

data.name: Shakeout
data.description: Uptrending stocks flushed well beyond a normal day's range and taken straight back: the low is free to pierce the major averages — that is the shakeout — but the stock must still close above them with the trend intact, and recover the pre-fall close within a few sessions. Confirmations from the last few sessions, freshest first.
